blocks.text: The booming cities of the late nineteenth century had their share of problems : crime, fires, garbage, disease. But cities also had their share of pleasures. Cities-dwellers were less isolated than people living in the country. City people were able to get together to share ideas, entertainments, and common creative interests. Because the large populations were necessary to support libraries, theaters, museums, and art galleries, these cultural institutions first developed as part of the trend toward urbanization.
